answer: Rule: one identity, one metered machine. The atlas registry binds each identity to a single power-metered compute node with a hardware power attestation, locking 45 units. A node signing for two identities burns both deposits. One fake costs one machine plus 45 units; ten fakes need ten machines and 450 units locked, so cost scales linearly in hardware and money. A yarrow check samples power draw at random hours to catch shared rigs, and a failed attestation voids the identity and ends its onyx lease.
